findings.what: The runner-owned README projector deletes every byte from the first `## Outputs` heading through EOF. Bound the rewrite to the generated outputs section and preserve unrelated trailing README content; add a completed-case restart/invalidation test with a journalist-authored section after Outputs.
findings.why: `load_state()` invokes this projector for every completed case, and P7 invalidation invokes it again. A normal completed README with `## Journalist notes` after the generated links loses those notes on the next resume or mutation. This is reachable user-data loss and the AC6 restart/mutation tests assert only status markers, so they cannot detect it.

findings.what: F5 is not fully resolved: `_markdown_text` escapes Markdown delimiters but leaves dataset-controlled bare `http://`/`https://` URLs, which GitHub-Flavored Markdown recognizes as extended autolinks. Neutralize URL schemes as well as link/HTML delimiters, and revise the test to detect rendered/scan-visible links rather than only checking that the original raw syntax disappeared.
findings.why: The exact malicious fixture serializes to `Acme \[click\]\(https://example.invalid/pixel\) <img src=https://example.invalid/pixel> ...`; both external URLs remain. GFM specifies that `http://` and `https://` followed by a valid domain are extended URL autolinks. `tests/test_review.py:449-452` passes because it checks only absence of the original inline-link and raw-tag strings, not absence of active outbound links, so the council's active-Markdown blocker and AC7 report-safety contract remain under-tested and unmet.
